newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium ends higher, copper drifts, tin firm.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium ends higher, copper drifts, tin firm.

text.p: Tight nearby backwardations and falling London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks helped to drive three months delivery aluminium higher by the close of business on Friday.
Elsewhere, unable to absorb a further LME stocks rise copper drifted, while tin on short-covering against the backdrop of uptrending charts moved to settle above $5,600 a tonne.
Traders said aluminium received a boost from further investment fund buying following a breach above expected resistance at $1,725.
Charts during the week, despite downside retracements, have pointed to higher levels amid continued LME inventory falls and consumer demand.
Last business was seen at $1,739, one dollar down on its 21-month high of but a gain of $38 from Thursday's LME kerb close.
Traders said they expected aluminium to test resistance at $1,750 in later trading on the back of covering from the U.S.
If the market manages to breach this level they expect further gains towards $1,775.
A narrowing of nearby spreads and a further inventory increase knocked copper lower to $2,309.50, down from $2,311.
The cash to three months spread was last at around a $5 backwardation, versus level on Thursday.
Traders said that the market now looks set to test $2,300 or lower next week. "Overall the market is lacking upside momentum its due to head lower," one market operator said.
Tin correcting from a recent oversold condition moved higher on short-covering and trade covering. It was last at $5,640, up $95.
Traders said a period of consolidation was likely and that the market needed to breach resistance at $5,690.

Nickel moved $55 higher to $7,485 on news that Falconbridge's 1,400 unionised workers at its Sudbury, Ontario operations are on strike after union and company negotiators failed to agree on a new contract.
Traders that the market rose but several believed that the news was already factored into the price of nickel.
"If the news was not already factored in we would have seen a gain of around $200," one trader commented.
Lead was quiet and settled at $639, versus $632.
Alloy was last quoted higher AT $1,540 against $1,515/25 following the rise in the primary market. --London Newsroom +44 171 542-8075
